owner: Platform Engineering · reviewed in source; owner content review pending
reviewed: 2026-11-14 · source model with separately dated deployment observations
disclosure: Sanitized identity reference · no credentials or private inventory

nodes.title: Platform foundation
nodes.purpose: Shared reference platform and proposed assessment scope.
nodes.usage: Explore the packages and management plane.
nodes.configuration: Platform Git owns shared configuration.
nodes.runbook: Validate target-specific readiness before adoption.

nodes.title: RKE2
nodes.purpose: Kubernetes runtime foundation.
nodes.usage: Hosts platform services and scoped tenant workloads.
nodes.configuration: Infrastructure Ansible owns provisioning inputs.
nodes.runbook: Review prerequisites, readiness and recovery before operating.

nodes.title: Flux
nodes.purpose: Reconciles reviewed desired state from Git.
nodes.usage: Reconciles reviewed immutable sources into desired platform and application state. Reconciliation success and actual application acceptance are separate.
nodes.configuration: Platform bootstrap selects sources and reconciliation scopes.
nodes.runbook: Review source identity and reconciliation evidence; this portal cannot reconcile.

nodes.title: Big Bang
nodes.purpose: Curates platform packages and their configuration.
nodes.usage: Select reviewed packages for the target.
nodes.configuration: Package values, prerequisites and pinned source belong in platform Git.
nodes.runbook: Render and test the actual selected packages before adoption.

nodes.title: Rancher · PE only
nodes.purpose: Platform engineering cluster lifecycle management.
nodes.usage: Reserved for authorized platform administrators.
nodes.configuration: Not an application GitOps owner or tenant UI.
nodes.runbook: Follow reviewed infrastructure guidance; no administrative controls here.

nodes.title: Keycloak
nodes.purpose: Shared identity provider and signed identity claims.
nodes.usage: Sign in to appropriately configured applications.
nodes.configuration: Each relying party validates audience, client, roles and group policy.
nodes.runbook: Review identity configuration and access tests; SSO alone grants no resource access.

nodes.title: Headlamp
nodes.purpose: Tenant-facing Kubernetes UI in the reference design.
nodes.usage: Inspect only resources authorized by Kubernetes RBAC.
nodes.configuration: Keep user identity and namespace permissions scoped; no token fallback.
nodes.runbook: Verify permitted and denied operations for the actual target.

nodes.title: OpenBao secrets authority
nodes.purpose: Source-backed secrets management with separate human and machine authentication.
nodes.usage: Authorizes access to scoped secret paths; this reference does not certify live deployment or recovery.
nodes.configuration: Review auth roles, KV policies, ESO delivery identity and recovery custody separately.
nodes.runbook: Validate unseal, backup/recovery and positive/negative access evidence; use the identity views for scope.

nodes.title: Example tenant boundary
nodes.purpose: Generic tenant scope; no real tenant inventory.
nodes.usage: Understand workload, data and responsibility separation.
nodes.configuration: Enrollment Git owns foundations; application Git owns deployments.
nodes.runbook: Require current positive and negative isolation evidence.

nodes.title: Tenant workloads
nodes.purpose: Application execution within a scoped tenant design.
nodes.usage: Use approved artifact identities and reviewed application configuration.
nodes.configuration: Namespace, service accounts and permissions require enforced policy.
nodes.runbook: Validate runtime, network, quota, admission and recovery boundaries.

nodes.title: Tenant data
nodes.purpose: Logical data scope with tenant-owned classification and retention.
nodes.usage: Store and access data through authorized applications.
nodes.configuration: Storage and backup policies require target-specific review.
nodes.runbook: Demonstrate restore and cross-tenant denial; namespace labels are insufficient.

nodes.title: PerkForge Portal
nodes.purpose: Visual documentation and a session-protected tenant directory.
nodes.usage: Explore sanitized documentation; sign in for your scoped workspace.
nodes.configuration: React + Fastify BFF; GitLab integration is disabled.
nodes.runbook: Run local checks; identity and deployment require separate review.

nodes.title: External image source
nodes.purpose: Untrusted upstream artifact origin for the proposed intake journey.
nodes.usage: Resolve an allowlisted source to immutable platform digests.
nodes.configuration: No imported image execution or Docker socket.
nodes.runbook: Reject missing coverage or identity drift.

nodes.title: GitLab CI + Trivy intake · planned
nodes.purpose: Proposed artifact-intake validation and CVE scanning pipeline, not the deployment status of GitLab itself.
nodes.usage: Scan every copied platform; retain SBOM and gate evidence.
nodes.configuration: Protected publisher separated from untrusted MR validation.
nodes.runbook: Fail on stale DB, findings per policy, errors, tampering or incomplete evidence.

nodes.title: Harbor intake publishing · planned
nodes.purpose: Proposed approved-intake publication workflow, not the deployment status of Harbor itself.
nodes.usage: Publish exact validated content through a protected publisher.
nodes.configuration: Scoped robot permissions and immutable tags require review.
nodes.runbook: Verify read-back digests; later rescans complement intake gates.

nodes.title: Credential custody
nodes.purpose: Protects bootstrap, node and signing credentials outside Git.
nodes.usage: Operators retrieve only the approved named credential for the task.
nodes.configuration: Owner-controlled encrypted custody; transient local sessions; no values in docs or images.
nodes.runbook: Lock sessions and remove transient signing material after use; validate rotation separately.

nodes.title: Node installer / operator
nodes.purpose: First authenticated actor on a fresh node.
nodes.usage: Bootstraps the OS and RKE2 using verified SSH and bounded privilege escalation.
nodes.configuration: Environment inventory chooses hosts; pinned host trust and node credentials remain separate.
nodes.runbook: Verify target identity before applying; do not treat a discovered address as trusted.

nodes.title: Node and cluster identity
nodes.purpose: RKE2 node registration and Kubernetes control-plane trust.
nodes.usage: Distinguishes bootstrap join authority, node certificates and operator kubeconfig.
nodes.configuration: Host preparation and RKE2 inputs govern registration; cluster credentials are not tenant credentials.
nodes.runbook: Review certificate/join credential lifecycle and recovery; not every lifecycle test is complete.

nodes.title: CA and service TLS
nodes.purpose: Authenticates service endpoints and the trust chain.
nodes.usage: Issue endpoint-scoped leaves and distribute only the required public trust.
nodes.configuration: Private signer stays in protected custody; TLS inputs are target-specific, not image rebuilds.
nodes.runbook: Verify hostname, intended usage, key match and renewal date; never disable verification.

nodes.title: Platform bootstrap identity
nodes.purpose: Installs foundational controllers and delegated service accounts.
nodes.usage: Applies the initial reviewed reconciliation and authorization foundation.
nodes.configuration: Bootstrap authority is distinct from later application installer and runtime identities.
nodes.runbook: Record privileges and retained recovery credentials; retirement is a separate gate.

nodes.title: GitOps source and deployer identities
nodes.purpose: Separates repository read credentials from Kubernetes write authority.
nodes.usage: Flux reads pinned source; reconciliation uses the selected scoped service account.
nodes.configuration: Platform, tenant control and runtime namespaces have distinct ownership and contracts.
nodes.runbook: Inspect exact source SHA, target scope and effective RBAC; Git review is not runtime enforcement.

nodes.title: Application installers / operators
nodes.purpose: Creates application prerequisites using explicit installer authority.
nodes.usage: Sets up clients, stores and owned resources before runtime activation.
nodes.configuration: Installers may need broader authority than the app; exceptions must remain visible and bounded.
nodes.runbook: Review cluster-wide Secret reads and delegated writes; no blanket claim that operators are least privilege.

nodes.title: Human identity and membership
nodes.purpose: Keycloak authenticates a person and emits signed claims.
nodes.usage: Platform groups and tenant groups represent distinct intended access scopes.
nodes.configuration: Each relying party validates its own issuer, audience, client and exact groups or native roles.
nodes.runbook: Test allowed and denied users, removal, session expiry and native app behavior independently.

nodes.title: Platform authority
nodes.purpose: Platform administrators are not tenant readers in disguise.
nodes.usage: The Portal accepts the exact platform-admin group without requiring a tenant role.
nodes.configuration: Administrative trust can bypass nominal tenant privacy; document that limitation explicitly.
nodes.runbook: Review platform-wide power, ordinary operations and emergency elevation separately.

nodes.title: Per-application authorization
nodes.purpose: Applications decide access after authentication.
nodes.usage: Maps identity to the supported native role, org, channel, path or query scope.
nodes.configuration: SSO alone does not grant resource ownership; service-specific enforcement remains necessary.
nodes.runbook: Validate revocation and cross-context denial; source readiness is not full live acceptance.

nodes.title: Tenant role and ownership
nodes.purpose: Tenant admins, developers and viewers are separate scoped roles.
nodes.usage: Defines only the authorized tenant namespace, data and collaboration context.
nodes.configuration: Parent groups grant nothing; control namespaces are not tenant runtime namespaces.
nodes.runbook: Complete native per-app lifecycle and cross-tenant tests before claiming the full model enforced.

nodes.title: OpenBao human / machine identity
nodes.purpose: Maps human OIDC or Kubernetes machine authentication to exact secret paths.
nodes.usage: Keeps authentication roles, KV policy and secret delivery separate.
nodes.configuration: Platform and tenant engines and paths have distinct authority; root recovery is not normal runtime.
nodes.runbook: Check policy and token lifecycle; metadata discovery is not secret-value access.

nodes.title: ESO delivery identities
nodes.purpose: Copies only reviewed secret records into owned Kubernetes destinations.
nodes.usage: Dedicated service accounts authenticate to OpenBao through scoped roles and stores.
nodes.configuration: Controller visibility can be broader than a store role; document both actual privileges.
nodes.runbook: Validate payload delivery, rotation and denial independently; a synced Secret is not rotation proof.

nodes.title: Pod / service account identity
nodes.purpose: Kubernetes service accounts identify workloads to authorized APIs.
nodes.usage: Use dedicated approved accounts rather than bootstrap or human credentials.
nodes.configuration: RBAC, token audience, admission and namespace policy work together; names alone are not isolation.
nodes.runbook: Check token mounts, exec/Secret/TokenRequest access and privilege changes through workloads.

nodes.title: Service credentials and mTLS
nodes.purpose: Applications use dedicated credentials for backend and publisher access.
nodes.usage: Keeps runtime protocols separate from human SSO and Kubernetes RBAC.
nodes.configuration: Bind credentials to exact routes/topics/paths; deliver through ESO rather than images or Git.
nodes.runbook: Validate least privilege, expiry and rotation; never expose values in the Explorer.

nodes.title: Recovery / break-glass
nodes.purpose: Separate emergency authority for recovery when normal identity paths fail.
nodes.usage: Retained bootstrap credentials and data access require explicit custody and accountability.
nodes.configuration: Routine identities must not silently inherit recovery privileges.
nodes.runbook: Document elevation, audit and retirement gaps; recovery design is not proof of every restore.

nodes.title: Future external workload trust
nodes.purpose: Federates tenant workloads to narrowly scoped external resource access.
nodes.usage: Design cloud trust and short-lived credentials for each workload, not a shared tenant cloud key.
nodes.configuration: Self-managed RKE2 is not automatically EKS Pod Identity or IRSA; provider trust must be designed.
nodes.runbook: Select and prove issuer/audience/subject binding, revocation and cross-tenant denial.

nodes.title: Future RDS / database identity
nodes.purpose: Database access is a separate authorization boundary from cloud API access.
nodes.usage: Define database users/roles, network access and supported IAM authentication separately.
nodes.configuration: Do not infer SQL permissions from cloud-role membership or assume all engines support the same flow.
nodes.runbook: Document connection and token lifecycle, least-privileged SQL grants and negative tests.

nodes.title: Deployment notification machine identity
nodes.purpose: Writes permitted native Helm outcomes to one approved topic.
nodes.usage: Keep machine publishing and human read rights separate; live delivery acceptance is distinct.
nodes.configuration: Dedicated scoped secret delivery; no tenant-wide source wildcard.
nodes.runbook: Verify denied reads/wrong topics and one genuine permitted event before closure.

nodes.title: Incident notification machine identities
nodes.purpose: Separate platform incident publishers from deployment publishers.
nodes.usage: Use exact audience/topic bindings, not general shared credentials.
nodes.configuration: Platform-owned runtime custody with separate records and scoped ESO consumers.
nodes.runbook: Review recipient entitlements and verify old routes after additive changes.

nodes.title: Mattermost operator / application identities
nodes.purpose: Native installer, application and human identities remain separate.
nodes.usage: Owner Keycloak login and private pilot channel visibility are verified; an independent native emergency administrator remains outside federation.
nodes.configuration: Closed signup and disabled temporary bootstrap access; shared platform team and private channels are platform managed. A reviewed, default-off membership adapter is not a deployed continuous controller.
nodes.runbook: Keep platform engineers, native emergency authority and tenant channel membership explicit. Do not infer continuous group synchronization or alert delivery from login acceptance.

nodes.title: Portal inventory artifact reader
nodes.purpose: Reads reviewed enrollment evidence without becoming a cluster controller.
nodes.usage: Keep source evidence distinct from deployed tenant health or mutable user management. Source-only application-pin and authenticated membership request previews perform no writes or persistence. Membership preview is default off, requires generic tenant-admin plus exact context (or independent platform-admin), and only proposes approved existing-subject developer/viewer membership. No snapshot is delivered; customer profiles/admin-role policy remain blocked, with an explicitly unsaved request-preview form disabled by default, not live CRUD. A source-only execution contract defines write-ahead audit/state transitions and uncertain-outcome readback; durable storage, authority and connected execution remain unimplemented.
nodes.configuration: Verified exact read-only ConfigMap mount of a pinned published-source baseline; no Kubernetes token or broad runtime API grant.
nodes.runbook: Verify artifact hash and runtime adapter separately from fresh user-interface acceptance. Never present this baseline as live cluster reconciliation state.

nodes.title: Logging installer identities
nodes.purpose: Keep reconciliation authority separate from collection and query identities.
nodes.usage: Existing scoped installers deploy the native backend and own-namespace collector operator.
nodes.configuration: Existing namespaced workload authority plus installer-only read-only node metadata listing and get of its one exact namespace. These metadata exceptions add no extra Secret, other-namespace, deployment-list or runtime permissions; existing Helm installer authority remains separate.
nodes.runbook: Verify rendered operator resources and effective namespace scope before marking collection accepted.

nodes.title: API-only scoped collector
nodes.purpose: Collect reviewed workload namespaces using trusted Kubernetes metadata.
nodes.usage: Real Mattermost and platform reconciliation logs now reach the scoped backend. The observed stage selects reviewed workload namespaces; application and platform reconciliation records are verified, while a quiet Portal workload had no observed records at the checkpoint. This is staged coverage, not all-cluster collection.
nodes.configuration: The collector may read pod metadata and logs cluster-wide, with get/watch on only its exact delivery credential Secret. It has no host mounts. Final trusted metadata chooses a registered ownership epoch or platform-only fallback; arbitrary pod annotations are not ownership authority.
nodes.runbook: Measure retries, drops, volume and storage before expanding collection. Initial credential-read denial caused a collection gap; later monitoring catch-up rejected historical timestamp-too-old batches. No lossless rollout or general redaction guarantee is claimed.

nodes.title: Authenticated logging gateway
nodes.purpose: Separate scoped write and read identities behind verified TLS.
nodes.usage: The active native gateway accepts the collector identity and serves platform read federation. Actual workload records are verified at the gateway; tenant query mapping remains disabled.
nodes.configuration: Four dedicated OpenBao records use exact-record ESO delivery to approved gateway, collector and query consumers. Legacy pilot reads remain separate. Server-fixed query scopes and explicit endpoint/method rules replace a shared write/query identity.
nodes.runbook: Verify reader/write denial, spoofed-header resistance and every tenant scope before exposing tenant access. Historical federation does not provide multi-tenant live tail. Existing volume and retention settings are unchanged; natural pruning and restore remain separate acceptance.

nodes.title: Grafana logging query identity
nodes.purpose: Read a platform federation through an organization-bound datasource.
nodes.usage: The organization-bound pod-log dashboard has verified chained namespace/pod/container queries and real log, volume and count panels through the read-only platform datasource. Default-All and selected-pod forms work, with all earlier dashboards preserved.
nodes.configuration: The platform datasource has a distinct read-only credential. The existing canonical engineer group now receives a dedicated Grafana-client entitlement mapped to platform-org Viewer; administrators retain separate global administration. No human memberships changed. Tenant org/session isolation remains a separate gated stage.
nodes.runbook: Verify both query APIs and actual user access. Newly ingested records have indexed pod labels; older structured-metadata records are not retroactively indexed. Interactive visual acceptance is separate; keep tenant exposure off until its server-side and session denial gates pass.

nodes.title: Namespace log-ownership guard
nodes.purpose: Keep a tenant log epoch bound to its approved runtime namespace identity.
nodes.usage: The Portal runtime namespace has a native admission guard. Ordinary deletion and changed context or epoch annotations are denied; unchanged metadata and existing foundation reconciliation remain allowed.
nodes.configuration: The guard pins the immutable namespace UID and two ownership annotations. Platform-owned policy is separate from tenant resources; trusted platform administrators can still alter it. No tenant query access is granted by this guard.
nodes.runbook: Before ownership transfer, revoke old query and session access, stop old routing and retire the epoch through explicit review. Never assign a previous owner’s log partition to a new namespace owner.

nodes.title: Portal checks and image build
nodes.purpose: Validate source and build the application image once.
nodes.usage: Push/PR checks and the image workflow run aggregate tests, dependency audit, a digest-pinned base build and a constrained runtime smoke test. PR/manual checks do not publish.
nodes.configuration: A main release saves the checked image artifact; the publishing job loads that exact artifact, verifies source/version tags and registry digest, and does not rebuild for the target environment.
nodes.runbook: A successful check is not a release or deployment. Verify the normal publisher and exact registry digest before a configuration pin.

nodes.title: Nextcloud SSO review and promotion
nodes.purpose: Separate a manually reviewed image build from authorized publication.
nodes.usage: Manual review builds from pinned application and OIDC inputs, verifies bundled dependencies, and saves a review artifact with hashes. A separate manually gated promotion consumes that reviewed artifact.
nodes.configuration: Promotion checks exact reviewed source, package visibility and publication guards, then promotes without rebuilding. Chart checks are a separate push/PR workflow.
nodes.runbook: A manual workflow definition or successful check does not mean publish=true or deployment. Keep promotion receipts and review the selected digest.

nodes.title: Application configuration releases
nodes.purpose: Carry immutable image references and deployment configuration separately from images.
nodes.usage: The Portal chart repository runs offline chart checks and versioned configuration releases. Nextcloud runs offline chart/SSO checks; its application-image promotion is separate.
nodes.configuration: Git release tags resolve to exact source commits. A configuration repository selects an already built digest; it does not rebuild the image or directly deploy a cluster.
nodes.runbook: Verify released chart inputs, digest and provenance before selecting the configuration in enrollment.

nodes.title: Enrollment validation and releases
nodes.purpose: Validate and version platform-owned enrollment selections and boundaries.
nodes.usage: Offline enrollment, Nextcloud candidate and Portal/ESO foundation workflows validate source and native admission fixtures. The configuration-release workflow creates reviewed versioned source releases.
nodes.configuration: Generated inventory, exact application configuration refs and runtime contracts travel in enrollment source. The foundation test workflow does not provision live credentials or activate resources.
nodes.runbook: Verify generated inventory freshness, native boundary tests and release tag-to-commit identity; a source release is not actual tenant CRUD or reconciliation.

nodes.title: Platform source release · checks paused
nodes.purpose: Select immutable enrollment and native package sources for GitOps.
nodes.usage: Platform configuration-release remains defined. Its reusable validation jobs and release-checks are explicitly paused in source; the main source-release job can still run despite skipped checks.
nodes.configuration: A workflow marked active by GitHub does not override job-level if:false. Skipped CI is not passing validation; reviewed local/native evidence must be stated separately.
nodes.runbook: Do not silently reactivate CI or claim a green platform gate. Verify exact reviewed source and live reconciler readiness independently.

nodes.title: Published immutable images
nodes.purpose: Store checked image bytes independently of target environment configuration.
nodes.usage: Portal publication and the gated Nextcloud SSO promotion use GHCR. Native Big Bang services consume selected upstream Registry One images rather than new PerkForge builds.
nodes.configuration: Version and source tags must resolve to the recorded digest. GitOps carries references; runtimes fetch image bytes from the registry. No target-specific rebuild is required.
nodes.runbook: Keep registry custody, source provenance, image availability and runtime pull access separate from a successful build.

nodes.title: Delivery inventory scope
nodes.purpose: Keep current source workflows distinct from planned or absent automation.
nodes.usage: The reviewed eight nonarchived repositories contain thirteen GitHub Actions workflow definitions and two image Dockerfiles. The operator-recovery, earlier UI and field-guide repositories have no checked-in Actions workflow.
nodes.configuration: This is a dated source/run-metadata inventory, not discovery of every external CI service. The proposed GitLab/Trivy/Harbor intake remains planned; no live GitLab job inventory was inferred.
nodes.runbook: Refresh workflow sources, triggers, active/job-level pause state and output references when delivery changes. Never equate an existing Dockerfile with an executing pipeline.

nodes.title: Paired application recovery capture
nodes.purpose: Capture files, database and required configuration as one consistent recovery generation.
nodes.usage: An application-aware capture pairs data with database and protected configuration, then records completion and integrity metadata. An incomplete run is not a recovery point.
nodes.configuration: Secrets remain in protected recovery custody, not source or the diagram. Scheduler health and a directory name are not evidence of a complete generation.
nodes.runbook: Verify completion, matching generation, required versions and available independent unlock material before using any artifact.

nodes.title: Independent copy and integrity
nodes.purpose: Keep a verified recovery copy separate from its source.
nodes.usage: A completed secondary copy has matching destination hashes. Copy integrity is verified separately from application recovery; a second local disk is not automatically off-site or another failure domain.
nodes.configuration: Keep paired artifacts and receipts together, verify lengths/hashes, and retain a read-only source or equivalent verified copy before replacing anything.
nodes.runbook: A skipped unchanged copy is not a new hash test. Missing, partial, conflicting or unexpected contents are stop conditions.

nodes.title: Isolated files and database restore
nodes.purpose: Restore without overwriting production or the only surviving recovery set.
nodes.usage: Use compatible application/database tooling, a new volume or writable working copy and a disposable database. Inspect source media read-only and prevent unintended journal replay.
nodes.configuration: Recreate only reviewed isolated configuration; do not blindly apply production manifests. Disable or isolate scheduled jobs, outbound mail/hooks, public ingress and real SSO callbacks.
nodes.runbook: Stop for unknown media layout, missing paired inputs or conflicting generations. A bounded restore from the primary set passed; application restore from the copied set remains untested.

nodes.title: Application recovery verification
nodes.purpose: Prove usable recovered data rather than just successful copying or database startup.
nodes.usage: The accepted bounded primary-set drill passed app/database startup and active-file size/hash checks. Secondary-copy hash verification is separate and does not prove that copied set boots.
nodes.configuration: Record capture identity privately, compatible versions, counts, hashes, exclusions, duration and errors. Browser identity, tenant isolation and complete service recovery are distinct checks.
nodes.runbook: Test representative important files and intended/denied access in isolation. Do not infer an RPO/RTO or whole-cluster pass from this limited drill.

nodes.title: Explicitly reviewed production cutover
nodes.purpose: Make a recovery result the production source only after a separate decision.
nodes.usage: Review recovery point and newer-data loss, downtime, desired-state ownership, storage/database references and identity before any replacement. This model performs no restore or cutover.
nodes.configuration: Preserve surviving production data and the recovery source. Apply reviewed source changes and verify app, access, alerts and backups afterward.
nodes.runbook: Cleanup only identified throwaway resources after confirming another valid copy; retain the evidence and do not hide a failed attempt.

nodes.title: Independent credential recovery
nodes.purpose: Make recovery materials accessible without depending on the failed cluster or live vault.
nodes.usage: Encrypted export and downloaded-copy verification are distinct from replacement-vault import or account recovery. The export password and recovery access must be independently available.
nodes.configuration: Do not make the service being restored the sole custodian of its own recovery keys. Backup verification does not prove every excluded item or required service credential was captured.
nodes.runbook: Stop if unlock material, recovery access or a required service input is missing. A full replacement-vault import remains untested.

nodes.title: Whole-cluster recovery dependencies
nodes.purpose: Show a generic dependency order, not a cluster-specific or tested disaster-recovery recipe.
nodes.usage: Recover source/artifact and credential/PKI access; re-establish hosts/network/DNS/time and supported control-plane recovery; then storage, identity/secrets, databases and applications.
nodes.configuration: Each service needs its own compatible state and recovery materials. Git desired state and one application backup do not restore control-plane, identity-provider or secret-service databases.
nodes.runbook: Require matching snapshots, tokens, versions, storage capacity and scoped access checks. Stop for missing inputs; whole-cluster restore, complete rebuild/HA and per-service recovery remain unverified.

views.title: Identity: install to tenant
views.summary: First review document: the complete identity lifecycle, from node installation to tenant workloads. Current means source-backed, not a live security certification.

views.title: Bootstrap & installer trust
views.summary: How node, platform and application installers hand authority forward. Bootstrap and recovery power are not runtime identities.

views.title: People & application access
views.summary: Authentication, platform authority and tenant scope are separate. Each app must enforce its native access model.

views.title: Secrets & workload identity
views.summary: Dedicated workload and secret-delivery identities today; external cloud and RDS identity is explicitly planned.

views.title: Current identity observations
views.summary: A reviewed operational snapshot, not automatic discovery. Consult the dated evidence and distinguish active, staged and source-only identities.

views.title: Logging identity and trust flow
views.summary: Trusted API collection → exact-record credential delivery → scoped gateway → platform datasource and pod-log dashboard. Real workload records, chained label/panel queries and dashboard preservation are verified; collection expansion and tenant exposure remain separate gates.

views.title: The whole platform
views.summary: A map of the reference design, from shared foundations to tenant workloads.

views.title: Inside the foundation
views.summary: Big Bang supplies packages. Flux reconciles applications. Rancher stays with platform engineering.

views.title: Identity is a starting point
views.summary: Keycloak supplies identity. Each application and Kubernetes enforce their own authorization decisions.

views.title: Platform authorization scope
views.summary: Proposed shared-platform assessment scope and dependencies. Scope remains subject to authorizing-official review.

views.title: Inside a tenant boundary
views.summary: A generic tenant scope with shared services outside it. A box does not enforce isolation.

views.title: From external image to workload
views.summary: External image → GitLab validation / Trivy → Harbor → Flux desired-state review → workloads. Flux carries references, while the runtime pulls bytes from Harbor.

views.title: Current pipelines and image builds
views.summary: Actual GitHub checks, manual image promotion, release tags, digest pins and GitOps are separate stages. Platform validation is paused; planned GitLab intake is not current automation. An image is built once and referenced across environments.

views.title: Backup and restore: generic flow
views.summary: Paired capture → verified independent copy → isolated restore → application proof → separately reviewed cutover. Primary-set bounded recovery passed; copied-set application restore and whole-cluster recovery remain unverified. No cluster identifiers or recovery secrets are modeled.

steps.title: Establish node trust
steps.body: Verify host identity, retrieve only approved credentials and apply the reviewed installation inputs.

steps.title: Bootstrap the platform
steps.body: Separate temporary installer authority from the controllers and service accounts it creates.

steps.title: Delegate reconciliation
steps.body: Pin the source and constrain the deployer. Git source credentials are not Kubernetes write privileges.

steps.title: Authenticate people
steps.body: Keycloak issues signed identity claims; each application validates the intended audience and authorization.

steps.title: Identify each workload
steps.body: Use approved service accounts and resource policy; avoid inheriting installer authority.

steps.title: Authenticate to the secret authority
steps.body: Map the machine identity to exact OpenBao paths; keep human and machine roles separate.

steps.title: Deliver owned secrets
steps.body: Synchronize reviewed destinations; test access and rotation, not only successful reconciliation.

steps.title: Extend trust deliberately
steps.body: Future cloud/RDS access needs its own federation and database authorization design. It is not deployed by this document.

steps.title: Resolve the source
steps.body: Allowlist source and destination. Resolve once to immutable manifest and runnable platform digests.

steps.title: Validate and scan
steps.body: Isolated GitLab jobs run Trivy for every copied platform. Missing coverage, stale databases, errors and policy failures block publication.

steps.title: Publish exact content
steps.body: A separately permissioned publisher verifies producer identity, gate evidence and hashes, then verifies Harbor read-back digests.

steps.title: Review desired state
steps.body: A reviewed Git change pins approved artifact references. Flux reconciles that desired state; it does not move image bytes.

steps.title: Run and verify
steps.body: The runtime pulls the approved digest from Harbor. Admission and runtime permissions still require separate validation.

steps.title: Enter the portal
steps.body: The browser holds an opaque secure session cookie. Access tokens stay in server memory.

steps.title: Verify identity and policy
steps.body: The BFF validates signature, issuer, audience, authorized client, API role and the configured exact group policy.

steps.title: Read scoped data
steps.body: The tenant BFF traverses bearer API validation. The adapter is disabled or fixture-only; no live GitLab requests occur.

identitySnapshot.notice: Reviewed snapshot, not automatic discovery or a live health feed. Source-only and staged changes are not deployed capabilities. Compiled Portal assets now require a verified session; distinct private role-specific models remain separate work. Later changes require evidence review and a Portal release.

records.title: Portal administrator identity
records.summary: Verified Portal access requires the exact signed platform-admin group, independently of tenant-reader membership. Runtime has no Kubernetes service-account token. Tenant creation and user administration are not enabled.

records.title: Platform deployment publisher and engineer reader
records.summary: Dedicated machine publisher writes only the platform deployment topic; the existing engineer subscriber reads it. Existing tokens were retained and ESO delivers one exact publisher Secret. ACL checks, genuine native success/failure publication and owner-confirmed phone receipt are verified. Only platform-namespace Helm releases are selected, not tenant Portal upgrades. Timestamp-varying native failures may still repeat.

records.title: Platform incident notification identities
records.summary: Separate machine publishers and exact-topic subscribers remain distinct from deployment notifications. Runtime credentials are platform-owned OpenBao records delivered by scoped ESO. Existing incident mounts and Portal identity remain preserved.

records.title: Mattermost identities and installer authority
records.summary: Native operator and application are ready, with closed signup. The owner verified Keycloak browser login and visibility of the private pilot channel in the shared platform team. A separate native emergency administrator is outside Keycloak; its credential is held in the approved password vault, and temporary bootstrap access is disabled. Grafana’s channel-locked receiver delivered a labeled native test, verified by channel readback and owner-confirmed visual receipt, while preserving the existing phone receiver. Production firing, recovery and repeat scenarios remain separate acceptance; continuous tenant membership reconciliation is not deployed. New private platform operational channels have exact role-based membership and owner-confirmed visibility; a one-shot adapter is not continuous reconciliation. The new tenant deployment channel remains recovery-only and its routing is not deployed at this checkpoint. Scoped relay credential delivery is staged, not message-delivery proof.

records.title: Portal enrollment inventory reader
records.summary: The released Portal now reads a verified, exact read-only inventory ConfigMap containing a pinned published-source baseline. Its declared application entries are not the cluster’s current root, reconciliation health, customer tenants or user administration. Existing deployer authority is constrained to the named inventory object by RBAC and admission. Runtime remains tokenless without added secret or network access. Adapter and anonymous API denial are verified; fresh owner inventory UI acceptance remains unverified.

records.title: External tenant workload and database trust
records.summary: Cloud workload federation and RDS/database authorization remain future design. They are not granted by a human platform-admin role or Kubernetes service-account name alone.

records.title: Scoped logging identities and custody
records.summary: The active native collector now reads selected real workload logs using a distinct writer identity; platform queries use a separate read-only federation. Four exact-record OpenBao/ESO consumers are synchronized. Gateway queries return real Mattermost and platform reconciliation records; Portal is quiet. The measured collection stage covers selected reviewed namespaces, not the whole cluster. A credential-read denial caused a rollout collection gap, so lossless delivery is not claimed. Tenant reader mapping remains disabled; full cross-scope denial, expansion capacity, natural retention, restore and comprehensive redaction remain separate acceptance.

records.title: Portal namespace ownership and epoch
records.summary: The native policy and Deny binding are live with typechecking accepted. Native server-side dry-runs accept unchanged metadata and foundation reconciliation, and reject ownership annotation removal, context/epoch changes and deletion. UID and existing namespace labels/security settings were preserved. This blocks ordinary namespace-name reuse while the guard remains bound; it does not prove tenant log authorization or prevent trusted platform administrators changing policy.

records.title: Scoped pod-log delivery transition
records.summary: The organization-bound platform datasource and native pod-log dashboard are active. All 41 existing dashboard UIDs are preserved. Actual namespace/pod/container queries and real log, volume and count panels passed through Grafana for both default-All and selected-pod forms. Newly ingested records now retain indexed pod labels; older records are not retroactively changed. The owner confirmed seeing pod logs in the dashboard; independent native query evidence remains separate from that visual acceptance. Tenant readers remain disabled pending cross-scope and identity/session denial checks; initial collection remains staged, not all-cluster coverage. The engineer-group entitlement and matching native org-Viewer configuration are live and read back; an actual engineer-only human login remains untested, distinct from native fixture coverage and administrator acceptance.

records.title: Grafana identity-provider transport
records.summary: Grafana reaches the existing identity provider through an explicitly selected ingress backend on its translated TLS port. The approved egress addition preserves all previous rules, TLS verification and client credentials. Trusted-TLS discovery and the token endpoint path were verified from the workload; the owner confirmed browser login. This transport repair neither assigns new human roles nor proves tenant datasource isolation.

revisionMeaning: platformRevision and portalRevision identify the original model-source references, not the deployed platform or Portal release. Per-node links identify source evidence; identitySnapshot records separately dated runtime observations.
